author: NorthEast News Desk
body: World Athletics is launching its inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest with the richest prize structure in the sport’s history. Winners of individual events will receive $150,000, while the winning relay teams will divide $80,000, creating a significant incentive for athletes at the new showcase meet.

Retired sprint champion Usain Bolt said the payouts would have attracted him during his career. A sprinter competing in the 100 meters, 200 meters and mixed 4x100 relay could contend for multiple awards across the program, although each event still requires qualification and victory against an elite field.

Organizers designed a streamlined schedule with less downtime, theatrical lighting and a black infield. World Athletics President Sebastian Coe described the championship as a place to test presentation changes while focusing attention on recognizable athletes and direct competition.

The experiment addresses a persistent challenge for track and field: major championships command broad audiences, but many meets struggle for attention between Olympic cycles. Bigger prizes and a compact format do not guarantee long-term success, but they give athletes a stronger financial reward and provide the governing body with a clear test of whether a faster, star-centered event can attract new viewers.
dek: Individual winners can earn $150,000 at the new Budapest meet, part of a faster presentation built around elite head-to-head events.
headline: Ultimate Championship debuts with record prize money for track
